content_record.title: Aging is a networked failure: mitochondria, circadian clocks, and oxygen delivery converge
content_record.editorial_body: A new special issue reframes aging as a multi-system process driven by shared mechanisms—mitochondrial dysfunction, circadian disruption, hypoxia, and inter-organ signaling—with vascular and immune shifts as upstream drivers. Mitochondrial dysfunction and circadian disruption are shared aging mechanisms. Vascular and immune shifts drive tissue decline across organs. Tissue microenvironments explain why aging trajectories differ. This signal is based on Aging as a Networked Process: Systems, Signals, and Interventions Across the Lifespan. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context.
